content: The World Health Organization (WHO) emphasizes that the designations and presentation of material in its publications do not imply any opinion regarding the legal status of countries, territories, cities, or their authorities, nor the delimitation of their borders. The interim guidance on managing Ebola events at points of entry (PoE), published in September 2014, was developed by WHO in collaboration with experts from WHO, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the International Air Transport Association (IATA), and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). This guidance is intended for National Focal Points for the International Health Regulations (IHR 2005), public health authorities at PoE, PoE operators, conveyance operators, crew members, and other stakeholders involved in managing public health events. It should be used alongside WHO publications on contingency planning at PoE, local emergency plans, and established capacities. The guidance recommends adapting its contents to the current situation, local requirements, and common practices. 1. For countries with Ebola virus disease (EVD) transmission: Conduct exit screening of all individuals at international airports, seaports, and major land crossings for unexplained febrile illness consistent with potential Ebola infection. 2. For all points of entry: For international airports, the aerodrome emergency plan should include a public health component in line with ICAO health-related requirements. Allocate a designated area at PoE for health assessments in case of suspected illness in travelers. Establish standard operating procedures for referring ill travelers to designated hospitals, including identifying adequate ambulance services. 3. Raise awareness among conveyance operators about the need to notify PoE health authorities immediately upon identifying suspected cases before arrival. Maintain effective and rapid communication between PoE health authorities and the national health surveillance system. During travel, potential cases may be detected at various points. Key actions include: Detecting and managing suspected cases at departure points, during transit, or upon arrival. Ensuring that symptomatic travelers are not permitted to travel unless as part of a medical evacuation. Activating public health emergency plans at PoE when necessary, arranging medical examinations, and transporting suspected cases to designated hospitals. Collecting clinical or environmental specimens as needed and ensuring their safe transport to appropriate laboratories. If the traveler has been in an EVD-affected area or in contact with a suspected or confirmed case, contact tracing should be conducted to identify close contacts, such as passengers seated nearby on the same flight. If a suspected case is identified, authorities should activate contingency plans, arrange for medical assessments, and supervise cleaning and disinfection procedures. Finally, after travel, individuals with symptoms consistent with EVD should seek medical care at a hospital.
